title: She Dreams in Blood
author: Fletcher, Michael R.
review:
There's definitely cool moments and interesting ideas in this book, more so than the first book. In isolation I like this one more than the first one. However overall as a series I'm souring on it.

The main character and first person POV is frustrating to read about. His internal struggle is just not compelling and his romance interests are fairly juvenile. The character development was poorly done, the plot didn't move far enough in this one. It's more about the spectacle here and the themes and overarching narrative are falling flat.

“Save yourself,” I said. “Now is not the time to be the hero.” He coughed a sputtering laugh, cracked lips seeping blood. “That’s what makes it the right time.”

By the late teens, most people already had their parent’s beliefs, foolish or otherwise, carved into their soul. It was hard to cut out such faith. People hate change. They fear being forced to think—or rethink—more than they’re afraid of being wrong or looking stupid.

“I’m at war with myself, damnit! I want to be a better man. I want to be a man who doesn’t cut throats to call demons, who doesn’t feed innocent souls to hellish creatures.” “Your actions say otherwise,” he said, glancing at NamKhar. “You are either a hypocrite, or a liar.”

“Stop pretending. You know who you are. You know what you are. You are the iron fist binding your fractious species together. You are their doom and their salvation. You are selfish and cruel. You crave power. You fear death, and more than anything, you fear being alone.”
I’ve been here three thousand years. Alone. I can be here one hundred thousand more. It’s nothing; I’m not human. Your world will die, and I won’t even notice.”
